text:
Maria: Heads-up — the Ruby quickstart has a copy/paste bug: the curl example uses "Auth: Bearer" instead of "Authorization: Bearer", which causes 401s for new users. Also the Ruby snippet is missing the require line.

Maria: Current README snippet:
```bash
# wrong (current README)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Auth: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

Maria: The Ruby client block also starts with `client = Redwood::Client.new(...)` but no `require` so copy/paste fails.

Devon: Ack — where is the file?

Maria: docs/quickstarts/ruby/README.md around line ~42. I'll open a PR to fix header and add `require 'redwood_inference'`.

Sam: FYI we renamed the gem earlier; confirm exact require name so we don't flip again.

Priya: Thanks @Maria. Can you also add a tiny CI smoke check that runs the curl snippet against staging and fails on 401 or wrong header name?

Devon: We can add a docs-snippet-lint job that parses code fences and validates header names and env var usage. Lightweight and useful.

Maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/1234 — changes: replace Auth -> Authorization, add `require 'redwood_inference'`, clarify env var name REDWOOD_API_KEY, and a note about the gem name.

docs-bot: Created issue #3421 for ruby quickstart header + require mismatch (reporter: Maria).

Sam: Suggest keeping the sample SDK call minimal; show idiomatic `client.chat.create(...)` without too much extra.

Priya: Also add a one-line in CONTRIBUTING.md about testing copy/paste snippets locally before merging. Small QA step will prevent these regressions.

Maria: I'll update the PR with the contributing note and a simple GH action that runs the curl against docs-staging.

Devon: Great — once CI passes let's merge. :thumbsup:

Maria: Merged and backported to the 1.0 branch. Leaving this thread for visibility on the lint job details.

Sam: Filed a separate ticket to standardize Ruby SDK require names across all examples.

Priya: Great catch, Maria — saves new users a lot of head-scratching. :heart:
